content.title: Rory McIlroy Masters live updates: Final round at Augusta National
content.text: Updated April 12, 2026, 7:21 p.m. ETRory McIlroy is the defending champion at the 2026 Masters Tournament.McIlroy is tied for the lead at 11 under going into the final round.He is in the final pairing and tees off at 2:25 p.m. ET alongside Cameron Young.McIlroy is attempting to become the fourth golfer to win the Masters in consecutive years.Last year at the Masters, Rory McIlroy finally won his Green Jacket a year ago after years of coming up short. The question entering Sunday was: Will he now win a second in a row at the 2026 Masters?McIlroy led by a tournament-record six shots after 36 holes and was tied with Cameron Young after 54 holes. Below is a shot-by-shot account of how the day went for McIlroy. Watch the Green Jacket ceremony for Rory McIlroyThe Masters official website has a live stream of McIlroy getting his second green jacket.Rory McIlroy's final round at 2026 Masters Rory McIlroy No. 18: Par (2 under today, 13 under overall, Winner)The par-4 18th is playing at 465 yards today, and Rory, playing driver, gets too quick. His drive has sliced right, into the pins between the 18th and the 10th fairways. He's so far right, in fact, that Trevor Immelman is saying he should play up the 10th fairway!After moving the patrons and gathering his thoughts, McIlroy hit a hooking 8-iron over the gallery and around the corner toward the green. The shot has come to rest in the greenside bunker short and left of the green. The ball appears to have plugged and then popped out. If he can get on the green, two putts will win him a second green jacket.He's safe. McIlroy's ball floats out of the sand and rolls about 15 feet past the cup. Playing quickly, Rory's putt rolls just behind the cup and stops just inches away. McIlroy marks his ball and lets Cameron Young play. He's bent down, taking in the moment, knowing he's about to win a second Masters."Rory is a rare repeat winner at Augusta!" cries Jim Nantz as the ball drops. Rory McIlroy No. 17: Par (2 under today, 13 under overall, solo lead)Statistically, 17 is playing as the hardest hole on the course today. No one has made a birdie here. Zero.McIlroy rips a low bullet cut and stops in the middle of the fairway. He's in the garden spot. From 151 yards out, McIlroy pulls a 9-iron and walks after it confidently, but the ball lands short and right, then bounds further right. He's not in a terrible spot, but that wasn't a good shot. Rory's pitch shot, for a moment, looked like it might drop, but the ball rolled past the right edge of the hole and stopped 2 feet past the cup. Rory makes the putt and is now walking to the 18th hole at Augusta National with a two-shot lead and just one hole remaining in the 2026 Masters. Rory McIlroy No. 16: Par (2 under today, 13 under overall, solo lead)Hitting 8-iron on the 181-yard par 3, McIlroy's ball comes in hot and bounces over the back-left portion of the green on one hop. His downhill chip will be lightning quick. However, Rory is opting to putt instead of chip the ball. Attempting to use the slope, McIlroy's putt is reminiscent of Tiger Woods' famous shot on 16 at the 2005 Masters as it bends to the right and rolls down the hill. But instead of stopping on the lip and then falling in, Rory's putt stops a few inches to the right. He taps in, happily, to make par and retain his two-shot lead. Scottie Scheffler made par on 18 and is finished at 11 under. Justin Rose made bogey on 17 and has fallen to 10 under. Rory McIlroy No. 15: Par (2 under today, 13 under overall, solo lead)McIlroy has birdied this hole every day so far, but his drive on the 550-yard par 5 sails to the right and into a stand of trees between the 15th and 17th fairways. With a two-shot lead, a birdie would be great, but it might not be necessary to win. What he can't do is find the water that guards the green or send his second (or third) shot too far and into the pond behind the green. From 211 yards out, Rory hits a controlled, punch shot across and down the fairway to give himself a better angle to the hole with his third. From 108 yards out, Rory's wedge shot comes up short and, for a moment, looked like it might peel back into the pond, but it stops after one forward hop. He's dry and has a lengthy birdie putt. Rolling the ball up the slope, Rory's birdie putt stops inches short and left of the cup. He taps in for a par to keep his two-shot lead over Scheffler, who is in the middle of the 18th fairway, and Justin Rose, who is playing the 17th. Rory McIlroy's No. 14: Par (2 under today, 13 under overall, solo lead)Rory obliterated his tee shot down the fairway of the 440-yard par 4. You couldn't walk in the fairway and drop it in a better spot. From 133 yards out with a sand wedge, McIlroy's ball hit some wind that he didn't anticipate. He's fine, in the middle of the green, but he's got a long birdie putt on a hole where he could have used the slopes and contours to get the ball close. From about 35 feet, Rory's left-to-right putt comes up about 1 foot short, and he taps in for a par. He's two shots ahead of a surging Scottie Scheffler, who is playing the 17th. Rory McIlroy's No. 13: Birdie (1 under today, 13 under overall, solo lead)Wow, Rory is looking like a repeat champion as he ripped what Trevor Immelman called "his best drive of the week." On the par-5, his 350-yard tee shot took most of the trouble out of play, and with a two-stroke lead, he put himself in a great position. Hitting an 8-iron, his shot went long and left of the hole, stopping on a downslope in a depression in the first cut. McIlroy opted to putt, aiming nearly 25 feet left of the hole. The slope grabbed the ball as it rolled and pulled it right, down the slope. Leading by two shots over Rose, Young and Tyrrell Hatton (who is in the house at -10), Rory's 8-foot birdie putt fell into the cup moments after Scottie Scheffler's birdie putt on 15 dropped. Rory McIlroy's No. 12: Birdie (1 under today, 12 under overall, solo lead)Is this the clincher for consecutive Green Jackets? Rory hit a great 9-iron and will have a 7-foot birdie putt to add to his one-stroke lead. McIlroy calmly buried the putt and now has a two-stroke lead as he strides to the 13th tee box. Rory McIlroy's No. 11: Par (even today, 11 under overall, solo lead)After a big drive, McIlroy safely played out well to the right, avoiding the same pitfalls that he jumped into on Saturday, when he splashed in the pond. He safely made par. Rory McIlroy's No. 10: Par (even today, 11 under overall, solo lead)As others are starting to fall around him, Rory suddenly looks much steadier as he made a routine par on the 10th hole. His drive was just a nip over 300 yards and his second shot was deep again and he lagged up close and tapped in for par. Rory McIlroy's No. 9: Par (even today, 11 under overall, tied for lead)After consecutive birdies, Rory looked free and strong on his drive off the ninth tee box. However, his putter has been a bot cold and he again missed a six-footer for birdie that could have been a huge swing. Rory McIlroy's No. 8: Birdie (even today, 11 under overall, one off lead)Don't look now, but while he looked tentative and flustered early, Rory's drive on No. 8 might have been his best swing of the day, even if it came a little left. After hitting it 349 yards, McIlroy ripped an incredible second shot and will have an eagle putt. His speed was good on the eagle attempt, just a little to the left of the hole. He tapped in for birdie (as did Young) and the two are both one shots behind Justin Rose. Rory McIlroy's No. 7: Birdie (1 over today, 10 under overall, one off lead)A big 325-yard drive from Rory left him only 118 yards to the green, and he struck his approach to seven feet. As Cam Young has fallen with consecutive bogeys, Rory dropped his birdie putt and is now just a single shot behind Justin Rose. Rory McIlroy's No. 6: Bogey (2 over today, 9 under overall, three off lead)This feels like it's slipping away quickly. Another errant shot from Rory, who bombed one off the back of the green on the 180-yard par 3. He tried to putt out of the fringe and it got caught up on the collar, meaning he had a 12-foot par putt, which he missed. Rory McIlroy's No. 5: Par (1 over today, 10 under overall, two off lead)A big drive had Rory right down the middle on this 495-yard par 5, but while his second shot was right on line, it was well short on the front of the green, with a back pin placement. Rory had a 29-foot birdie putt but missed and tapped in for par. Rory McIlroy's No. 4: Double-bogey (1 over today, 10 under overall, two off lead)Ouch. Turning point? Been a rough start for Rory, who was wide of the bunker on the fourth hole, a 240-yard par 3. He chipped close and had a makeable par putt, but missed it and then lipped out his short put coming back to fall two shots off the pace. It's a catastrophic moment for McIlroy, who clearly looked uncomfortable standing over his bogey putt. Rory McIlroy's No. 3: birdie (1 under today, 12 under overall, tied for lead)Again, Rory found a bunker, this time as he went for the green on the 350-yard hole. His second shot out of the bunker got to about 15 feet, and he'll have a reasonable birdie putt. He drained the putt to get back into a tie with Young. Rory McIlroy's No. 2: Par (even today, 11 under overall, one stroke back)On his drive on the par-5 second, Rory put it in the bunker. He hit safely out of the deep fairway bunker to 96 yards away. On his third shot, he hit an approach that slid down to nine feet, but he missed the putt. Since Young made his birdie putt, Rory now trails by one stroke. Rory McIlroy's No. 1: Par (even today, 11 under overall)Rory opened the day on Saturday with a bogey at this par 4, and has not made birdie here all week. On Sunday, he boomed a drive in the fairway, but his iron was just a touch long and sat up on a ridge just a few inches from nestling right back to the cup. He had an 11-foot putt for birdie, but missed it and tapped in for par. Who will win the Masters? Rory McIlroy had long range session after third roundRory McIlroy is fighting a case of the lefts and if he wants to repeat as Masters champion, he will need to fix it before the final round.That’s why McIlroy hightailed it to the range after conducting his post-round press conference on Saturday. It is tradition for the leader to do his question-and-answer period at the press center but McIlroy’s manager requested that his man speak at a podium outside of scoring instead so McIlroy could work on his game before darkness fell.Here's more from our Adam Schupak, who is on location.Of course, one of his biggest mistakes on Saturday came when he pulled a shot left. We're guessing McIlroy will play No. 11 well right today:What was Rory McIlroy's Champions Dinner?As the reigning champion, McIlroy had the privilege of organizing the famous Masters Champions dinner on Tuesday before the tournament. Here's what he put on the menu:Appetizers: Peach & Ricotta Flatbread (balsamic, hot honey, basil); Rock Shrimp Tempura (creamy spicy sauce); Bacon-Wrapped Dates (goat cheese, almonds); Grilled Elk Sliders (caramelized onion jam, roasted garlic aioli)First course: Yellowfin Tuna Carpaccio (foie gras, toasted baguette, chives)Main course: Choice of Wagyu Filet Mignon or Seared Salmon (traditional Irish champ, sautéed Brussels sprouts, glazed carrots with brown butter, crispy Vidalia onion rings)Dessert: Sticky Toffee Pudding (vanilla ice cream and warm toffee sauce) When Rory McIlroy is in lead after 54 holes at a majorHere's a look at majors when Rory McIlroy was at least in a tie for the lead heading into the final round:MajorYear54‑hole positionFinal‑round scoreFinal resultMasters Tournament2011Solo lead (4 shots)80T‑15U.S. Open2011Solo lead (8 shots)69WonPGA Championship2012Solo lead (3 shots)66WonOpen Championship2014Solo lead (6 shots)71WonPGA Championship2014Solo lead (1 shot)68WonOpen Championship2022Tied for lead703Masters Tournament2025Solo lead (2 shots)73Won (playoff) Rory McIlroy has had major collapses, tooAlthough Rory McIlroy certainly has had his share of highlights, especially when leading major tournaments, McIlroy has also had some legendary collapses. Here's a look at a few, thanks to Charles Curtis from For The Win.2011 Masters: This one was agonizing. He entered Sunday at Augusta up four strokes and had a one-stroke lead with the back nine ahead. Then? A triple-bogey on 10 started a downward spiral that ended with him carding an 80 and finishing T15.2022 British Open: He came into Sunday with a share of the lead at the 150th Open Championship and was up two strokes at the turn. Then? He couldn't close and finished third.2024 U.S. Open: He was right there at Pinehurst with a bunch of missed short putts that left him with bogeys late after entering the final four holes with a one-stroke lead. Bryson DeChambeau took the title instead.2026 Masters: Blowing a six-shot lead could mean this performance ends up on this list permanently.Rory McIlroy seeks second Green JacketMcIlroy is the defending Masters champion and is seeking to become just the fourth to win the tournament in consecutive years. Jack Nicklaus, Nick Faldo and Tiger Woods were the first. Woods won his back-to-back in 2001 and 2002. Rory McIlroy's thoughts heading into SundayHere's what Rory McIlroy said after the third round about playing this year's final round:"I'd like to think that I'll play a little bit freer and I'll play, you know, like I've already got a green jacket, which I do. Sometimes I maybe just have to remind myself of that, but I think as well that the stakes in terms of, like, the pairing will be just a little bit easier. You know, the atmosphere out there will be a little bit easier."Yeah, I'm not worried about that at all. I wish I was a few shots better off, but I'm comfortable. I played with Cam the first two days. Playing with him again tomorrow. I think it's a comfortable group for both of us." What company would Rory McIlroy join with a win?In 2025, McIlroy won the Green Jacket to become just the sixth golfer to ever complete the Career Grand Slam by winning all four majors. But if he wins the Masters again this year, he'd join company even rarer than that. Here's a look at the three players who have won back-to-back Masters titles in the history of the iconic event.Jack Nicklaus (1965, 1966): Nicklaus dusted the field at the 1965 Masters, shooting 64 on Saturday and 69 on Sunday to finish 17 under and win by nine shots over a tie for second between Arnold Palmer and Gary Player. The following year was a much different story, but it produced the same result. Nicklaus, Tommy Jacobs and Gay Brewer all finished at even par, forcing an 18-hole Monday playoff in which Nicklaus fired 2-under 70 to secure his second straight Masters victory, while Jacobs shot 72 and Brewer blew up with a 6-over 78.Nick Faldo (1989, 1990): Faldo entered the final round of the 1989 Masters in a tie for ninth before charging up the leaderboard on Sunday with a 7-under 65, forcing a sudden-death playoff with Scott Hoch. Faldo and Hoch both bogeyed the 10th on the first playoff hole before Faldo made birdie at No. 11 to secure his first Green Jacket. The following year, Faldo found himself in another sudden-death playoff, this time with Raymond Floyd. Faldo went par-par on Nos. 10 and 11 in the playoff to defeat Floyd and become the second back-to-back Masters winner.Tiger Woods (2001, 2002): Woods is the most recent player to win consecutive Green Jackets. In 2001, Woods shot under par in every round of the tournament, finishing 16 under to win by two shots over David Duval. The next year at Augusta National saw a very similar result, as Woods once again finished every round under par, including a 66 on Saturday, to finish the week 12 under and three shots clear of the field, securing his second straight Masters title and his third of five in his career.Where to watch the final round of the 2026 MastersFeatured groups and featured holes coverage starts at 10:15 a.m. ET on Masters.com, the ESPN app, Paramount+. The streaming service has two hours of early-round coverage on the weekend before CBS takes over for five hours.Paramount+: 12-2 p.m. ETCBS/Paramount+: 2-7 p.m. ET New book on Rory highlights relationship with caddieIn a newly released biography, "Rory: The Heartache and Triumph of Golf’s Most Human Superstar," author Alan Shipnuck steps back even further, tracing McIlroy’s story to its roots — shaped by working-class parents, steadfast loyalty and relationships that have grounded him through golf’s brightest stages and darkest moments.As McIlroy returns to Augusta National in pursuit of the rare feat of back-to-back green jackets, Golfweek has partnered with Simon & Schuster to present an exclusive excerpt from Shipnuck’s book. The selection zeroes in on one of the most defining relationships of McIlroy’s career: his bond with longtime caddie and childhood friend Harry Diamond, and the quiet reliance McIlroy — famously the lone voice on his team — placed on that friendship in the crucible of Masters Sunday, during the final moments that sealed his long-awaited triumph.Here's the full excerpt.
